text.p: Despite signing for English side Blackburn from next season, Sampdoria's Swedish coach Swedish coach Sven Goran Eriksson says his future is still uncertain.
Speaking on Italian radio on Monday, a day after his side had beaten champions AC Milan 3-2 at the San Siro, Eriksson said:
"I'll be leaving Sampdoria at the end of the season...Two months ago, I signed for Blackburn and we announced that and nothing has changed since then.
"However, what exactly the future will hold, we'll see at the right time. I don't want to make any further comment on this...You never know what will happen in life..."

Italian sports media last week suggested that Eriksson, whose successful coaching career has included spells at Roma, Fiorentina and Portugal's Benfica, now wished to opt out of his agreement with Blackburn in order to take over at Rome club Lazio.
Last week Lazio sacked Czech coach Zdenek Zeman, replacing him with caretaker coach Dino Zoff, who will handle the side until the end of this season.

Italian media reported that Eriksson wanted to back out of the agreement with Blackburn because of family problems, suggesting that the coach preferred to remain near his daughter, a university student in Florence where she lives with Eriksson's estranged wife.

When it came to assessing Sampdoria's league title chances, Eriksson struck a cautious note despite the fact that Sunday's win against Milan closed the gap on league leaders Juventus to just two points.
"In August nobody expected us to be where we are now and it's obvious that everything is positive for us just at the moment...let's hope it can last like this.

"But the championship title is a long way off. When both Juventus and Sampdoria are at full strength, then we can match them, particularily at the moment, but I think that Juventus have a much stronger overall squad than us..."
Eriksson said speculation about his own future and about that of captain Roberto Mancini and French midfielder Christian Karembeu had had no negative effect on the side.
Last autumn Mancini came close to moving to Internazionale while Karembeu was involved in a three way tug-of-war between Sampdoria and the Spanish clubs Real Madrid and Barcelona.
"We've had a number of distractions this year, including me, Karembeu and Mancini, but the side has never suffered from this and has continued to do its business...
"We never talk about these things in the dressing room and we're all agreed to do our best both for Sampdoria and for ourselves right to the end of the season...
Eriksson also attributed the side's successful run to the club's ability to find good replacements for players such as Dutchman Clarence Seedorf and striker Enrico Chiesa, both sold last summer.

"We found the right players during the summer. We have a number of players here who I confess I didn't think would be as good as they have turned out, players like (Frenchman Pierre) Laigle, (Argentine Juan) Veron and (Vincenzo) Montella."
